paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God meets you right where you are, and where you are is not a mistake. Paul says it three times in this passage, and when a man says something three times, he wants it to land. "Each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called" (1 Corinthians 7:20). Married, single, married to someone who doesn't believe, doesn't matter. God called you in the middle of your life, and He can use the middle of your life.

Look at how Paul handles marriage. He says each person has "his own gift from God; one has this gift, another has that" (1 Corinthians 7:7). He also tells apart what the Lord commands and what he says himself, like "(I, not the Lord)" in 1 Corinthians 7:12. That's a man who is careful with God's words, and I LOVE that. And when a believer's unbelieving spouse leaves, he says "God has called you to live in peace" (1 Corinthians 7:15), so I think God cares about the weight you're carrying.

Then Paul zooms out to something bigger than marriage. "You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men" (1 Corinthians 7:23). Whether you're free or a slave, married or not, you belong to the Lord, and that's the thing that counts. So bake where you're standing, baker. Keep "God's commandments" (1 Corinthians 7:19), stay faithful in your own kitchen, and trust the One who called you there.
